name: Balanced 4-4-1-1

slots.why: Distributes to a compact block; plays it long or short depending on the pressure.
Support full-back gives width behind the wide midfielder without leaving the defence exposed.

Central defender in a balanced back four. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: slightly more direct passing does not ask the pair to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: slightly more direct passing does not ask the pair to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Wide midfielder is the safer side: he helps his full-back and keeps the shape compact.
Defensive central midfielder protects the back four and lets his partner go forward.
Supporting central midfielder links the defence to the attacking midfielder and striker.
Winger is the more attacking side, so the team has one safe flank and one creative flank.
Attacking midfielder plays behind the striker, linking play and arriving late in the box.
Lone striker: Advanced Forward runs in behind, Poacher stays in the box.

description: A conventional 4-4-2 defensive shell with one attacker dropping into the number-ten line to connect midfield and the lone striker.
whyGood: The AMC reduces striker isolation while preserving two clear banks of four without the ball.
whyThisShape: A 4-4-1-1: a flat back four and midfield four with a striker and a second player sitting just behind him. It keeps the compact shape of a 4-4-2 but gives the striker a link player, so the team is a little more creative than a plain 4-4-2 without losing its shape.
whenToUse: When you have one good striker and a creative player who is not a natural second striker, or as a steady all-round system for a mixed squad.
whenNotToUse: When you need two players to attack the box, or against sides that overload the middle: two central midfielders can be outnumbered.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
